decision: Keep the current default. The 128-token configuration passes correctness, but this workload loses throughput and worsens long-request TTFT and short-request p95 ITL. Do not promote it from this pilot.

plan.purpose: Measure whether smaller chunks reduce short-request inter-token stalls, and quantify any long-prefill/throughput cost. No SLO or release acceptance claim.

metric_scope: Report every measured request TTFT and every inter-token interval.

cache_followup.correction: The earlier allocator-fix/glm-cache-gap-review.json prose understated the routed expert domain. Current independent source and backend weights both declare288experts, partitioned0..255/256..287 by original execution; top8. Preserve all288.
findings: Public cache config already carries expert count and dimensions, but CUDA create/bind/begin/group/admission/close still hardcode512/top10. Bank geometry itself already supports1..512experts and1..32top-k.

Fixed512-sized masks and private arrays can remain bounded capacities; every active loop, key stride, offsets endpoint, offsets copy and integer-overflow check must use the declared count and top-k. GLM requires289offsets; reading513would overrun its metadata.
Compact cache slots over42MoE layers using a backend-owned mapping from physical model-layer IDs. Dense layers must not consume fictitious expert capacity or acquire leases.
GLM backend resources currently own no expert cache. Add cache ownership with staged preparation and rollback, preserving request/model lifetimes. Keep CPU-visible model weights free of GPU handles.

GLM request memory planning must charge the extra pinned/device raw-pointer arrays from cache binding; main memory accounting already reserves the requested GPU-cache budget separately. Preserve retained idle accounting.

GLM generic MoE work currently differs from Flash-specific cache orchestration. Single and grouped execution need route-complete layer lease acquisition, owner/peer rules, all-consumer fences, cancellation and failure poisoning before cache admission can be enabled.
Quant format payload sizing already uses registry capabilities through bank_pair_bytes; preserve existing Q4_K/Q5_K gate and Q5_K/Q6_K down arithmetic without new family branches in quant kernels.
acceptance: Keep existing512/top10Flash cache tests and references unchanged.
Test288/top8 cache hits, misses, eviction, exact289-entry offsets, expert287, overflow rejection, cross-domain bind rejection, pending layers, cancellation and shared consumers.
Qualify GLM whole-model heads against unchanged independent sources, normal and ASAN, multiple histories and reused sessions, with caches disabled and enabled.
Verify managed retained/idle bounds and separately measure physical memory; reconcile actual transfers and exposed stalls before performance claims.

implementation_entrypoints.single_request: src/transformer/bf16.c: bn_transformer_bf16_moe_begin/submit and GLM prepare/storage planning
implementation_entrypoints.geometry_regressions: Existing tests use implicit512/top10. Preserve them and add explicit288/top8 with an exactly289-entry offset buffer and expert287.

lifetime_requirements: Acquire route-complete layer tickets before bank fills. Cache hits must ignore poisoned staging and avoid source reads.
Grouped leases pin the unique union and preserve per-request offsets; finish all consumer streams before reuse.
Cancellation, participant-first teardown, source failure and partial upload must invalidate unpublished entries without losing retained-budget charges.
A compact42-MoE-layer index must map back to original physical layer IDs for source reads/preload; dense layers cannot be silently assigned expert keys.

limitations: Two closed-loop processes, one warmup pair and four measured pairs each, using two histories and reused client IDs; not sustained or open-loop SLO qualification.
Each geometry uses its own independent original-operator BF16 chronological profile. Continuation IDs differ, so this is not identical teacher-forced routing.
Logical upload counters are not reconciled PCIe transfer measurements. Events do not isolate CPU I/O, transfer stalls or GPU kernel time.
GPU physical peak was not sampled during timing. Managed payload limits and observed CPU wait4 high-water marks have different scopes.
Clocks are unlocked and process order is sequential. Source files are warm after hashing; no cold-I/O claim.
GLM GPU expert admission is still unsupported. The next change must handle288experts/top8and42MoE layers after3dense layers, with leases, cancellation, failures and memory accounting.
